speaker: Unknown
en: Ramp is the only platform built to make your finance team leaner, faster, and better, saving businesses 5% annually on average so you can stay focused on growth.
zh: Ramp 是唯一一个旨在让你的财务团队更精简、更快速、更优秀的平台,平均每年为企业节省 5% 的成本,让你能专注于增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ramp just opened for business in the United Kingdom, so if you're running a business in the UK, you can now use Ramp's AI-powered finance platform to manage cards, expenses, bills, approvals, and accounting all in one place.
zh: Ramp 刚刚在英国正式开业,所以如果你在英国经营企业,你现在可以使用 Ramp 的 AI 驱动财务平台,在一个地方管理卡片、开支、账单、审批和会计。

speaker: Unknown
en: I run my business on Ramp and so should you.
zh: 我用 Ramp 经营我的企业,你也应该用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Learn more at ramp.com slash invest.
zh: 在 ramp.com slash invest 了解更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: OpenAI, Cursor, Anthropic, Perplexity, and Vercel all have something in common.
zh: OpenAI、Cursor、Anthropic、Perplexity 和 Vercel 都有一个共同点。

speaker: Unknown
en: They all use WorkOS.
zh: 它们都在使用 WorkOS。

speaker: Unknown
en: And here's why.
zh: 原因如下。

speaker: Unknown
en: To achieve enterprise adoption at scale, you have to deliver on core capabilities like SSO, SCIM, RBAC, and audit logs.
zh: 要实现大规模的企业级采用,你必须交付核心能力,比如 SSO、SCIM、RBAC 和审计日志。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's where WorkOS comes in.
zh: 这就是 WorkOS 的用武之地。

speaker: Unknown
en: Instead of spending months building these mission-critical capabilities yourself,
zh: 与其花几个月时间自己构建这些任务关键型能力,

speaker: Unknown
en: You can just use WorkOS APIs to gain all of them on day zero.
zh: 你可以直接使用 WorkOS 的 API,在第一天就获得所有这些能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why so many of the top AI teams you hear about already run on WorkOS.
zh: 这就是为什么你听到的这么多顶级 AI 团队已经在 WorkOS 上运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: WorkOS is the fastest way to become enterprise ready and stay focused on what matters most, your product.
zh: WorkOS 是让你达到企业就绪状态并专注于最重要事情——你的产品——的最快方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Visit WorkOS.com to get started.
zh: 访问 WorkOS.com 开始使用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Rogo is the AI platform purpose-built for financial institutions, serving tens of thousands of bankers and investors at hundreds of leading firms worldwide.
zh: Rogo 是专为金融机构打造的 AI 平台,服务着全球数百家领先公司的数万名银行家和投资者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Rogo's AI agents autonomously execute large chunk of your firm's workflows.
zh: Rogo 的 AI 智能体自主执行你公司工作流中的大部分内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: They can screen deals, draft SIMs, run buyer outreach, and do diligence on data rooms, all with full security and compliance handled.
zh: 它们可以筛选交易、起草 SIM、开展买方外联、对数据室做尽职调查,全部都有完整的安全与合规保障。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every action feeds Rogo Intelligence, the firm's context layer, turning years of deal experience into a secure, governed institutional memory that makes each new transaction stronger than the last.
zh: 每一个动作都会输入 Rogo Intelligence——公司的上下文层,把多年的交易经验转化为安全、受治理的机构记忆,让每一笔新交易都比上一笔更强。

speaker: Unknown
en: To learn more, visit rogo.com slash invest.
zh: 想了解更多,请访问 rogo.com slash invest。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a very interesting thing happening that relates to a piece of your work, which I haven't seen you talk about as much.
zh: 有一件很有意思的事情正在发生,它与你工作中的一部分相关,而我不太见你谈论过这部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so maybe it's a fun place to begin, which is that it feels like we're now bandwidth limited on the most talented people's ability to do work.
zh: 所以也许这是个有趣的起点,那就是感觉我们现在在最优秀人才的做事能力上受到了带宽限制。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like it used to be that the rest of the world couldn't keep up with the most talented people.
zh: 就好像过去是其他世界跟不上最有天赋的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so they would get frustrated that no one was moving as fast or as efficiently as they were.
zh: 所以他们会因为没有人像他们一样快速或高效地推进而感到沮丧。

speaker: Unknown
en: There seems to be something flipping, which is actually some of these people would earn a really high return if they could generate more energy, maintain more energy, not burn out.
zh: 现在似乎有些事情正在翻转,实际上这些人如果能产生更多能量、维持更多能量、不把自己耗尽,就能获得非常高的回报。

speaker: Unknown
en: I heard this from several great entrepreneurs this summer that I think maybe Elon has just gotten into everyone's head that the real greats are going to run multiple companies.
zh: 今年夏天我从几位优秀的创业者那里听到了这个说法,我想也许 Elon 已经让所有人脑子里都形成了一个观念,即真正顶尖的人会同时经营多家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Technology unlocks so much potential for the most talented people.
zh: 技术为最有天赋的人解锁了如此多的潜力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this seems like an actual bottleneck is like these people's energy.
zh: 所以这看起来像一个真正的瓶颈,就是这些人的能量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'd be curious in all your research and study what you've learned about the component parts of this, like generating energy, maintaining it, clean versus dirty fuel, long-term performance.
zh: 我很好奇,在你所有的研究和学习中,你关于这方面的组成部分学到了什么,比如产生能量、维持能量、清洁燃料与肮脏燃料、长期表现。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like all of these things are fascinating and I think actually important to the degree of progress.
zh: 所有这些都很迷人,而且我认为实际上对进步的程度很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I would love you to just riff on all that for a while.
zh: 所以我希望你能就这些随便聊上一会儿。

speaker: Unknown
en: With the caveat that Elon represents the apex of being able to do multiple huge things simultaneously.
zh: 先说明一点,Elon 代表了能够同时做多个巨大事情的巅峰。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I don't think he has any peers in that regard.
zh: 我认为在这方面他没有任何同行者。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, one of the best multi-billionaire investors from the Bay Area who may have gone to Stanford and may have been part of the PayPal early team has asked me, how is it that Elon does this?
zh: 事实上,湾区最优秀的亿万富翁投资人之一——他可能上过斯坦福,可能曾是 PayPal 早期团队的成员——问过我,Elon 是怎么做到的?

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm like, I can't tell you.
zh: 我说,我没法告诉你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like physiologically.
zh: 比如从生理上讲。

speaker: Unknown
en: Physiologically, I mean, there are examples throughout history of people who seem to require less sleep.
zh: 从生理上讲,历史上有很多例子,有些人似乎需要更少的睡眠。

speaker: Unknown
en: They just have more energy and most people can get their energy up.
zh: 他们就是有更多能量,而大多数人可以把自己的能量提上来。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are a lot of healthy ways to do that now.
zh: 现在有很多健康的方式可以做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think now we've undergone this huge shift whereby everyone understands you have to sleep eventually and you have to know your own sleep requirements.
zh: 而且我认为现在我们已经经历了这个巨大的转变,即每个人都明白你最终必须睡觉,而且你必须了解自己的睡眠需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: So to dilute oneself into thinking you only need four or five hours because Elon only needs four or five hours, that's ridiculous.
zh: 所以稀释自己、以为自己只需要四五个小时,因为 Elon 只需要四五个小时,那是荒谬的。

speaker: Unknown
en: An honest self-assessment about how much sleep one actually needs to perform well
zh: 对自己实际需要多少睡眠才能表现良好进行诚实的自我评估,

speaker: Unknown
en: And perhaps best and what you can get by on.
zh: 或许还有最好的状态,以及你勉强能应付的睡眠量。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you can't get that, that's an important thing to understand.
zh: 如果你达不到那个量,这是需要理解的重要事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: But most people know, like for me, it's seven hours, I feel great.
zh: 但大多数人心里有数,比如对我来说,睡七个小时,我感觉很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: Eight probably puts me into the day a little bit groggy.
zh: 八个小时可能会让我这一天有点昏昏沉沉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Six, I can manage just fine.
zh: 六个小时,我完全可以应付。

speaker: Unknown
en: Five for one day or a sleepless night, I'm good.
zh: 五个小时撑一天,或者一个不眠之夜,我没问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Two nights like that,
zh: 两个这样的夜晚,

speaker: Unknown
en: Of four to zero hours of sleep and I'm cratered.
zh: 睡眠四小时到零小时,我就会垮掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think most people are similar.
zh: 而且我想大多数人都差不多。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's really changed is that we have effective, healthy ways to build our energy up.
zh: 真正改变的是，我们现在有了有效、健康的方式来提升自己的能量。

speaker: Unknown
en: We know to sleep, we can talk about exercise, caffeine.
zh: 我们知道要睡觉，我们可以谈谈锻炼、咖啡因。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some people are using nicotine.
zh: 有些人在使用尼古丁。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, it's addictive.
zh: 是的，它会成瘾。

speaker: Unknown
en: It raises blood pressure, but it does put people into that focused, but relaxed mode.
zh: 它会升高血压，但它确实能让人进入那种专注而放松的状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: I always say, if you really want the benefits of nicotine, don't use it very often.
zh: 我总是说，如果你真的想要尼古丁的好处，就不要经常使用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you want the actual cognitive enhancing effects or the focus enhancing effects,
zh: 如果你想要真正的认知增强效果或专注力增强效果，

speaker: Unknown
en: Then you have to not be a chronic user and then spike your system with nicotine at low amounts every once in a while.
zh: 那你就不能是一个长期使用者，而是每隔一段时间用低剂量的尼古丁给你的系统来一次脉冲式刺激。

speaker: Unknown
en: Setting Elon aside with the understanding that he represents that extreme in terms of energy and sleep requirements being very low, I think what's really happening now is people are hopefully doing this self-assessment.
zh: 把 Elon 放在一边——前提是要理解他代表着能量和睡眠需求极低的那种极端——我认为现在真正在发生的事情是，人们有望在做这种自我评估。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, I would hope people would have an honest conversation about themselves and say, at this point in my life...
zh: 比如，我希望人们能和自己进行一次诚实的对话，说，在我人生的这个阶段……

speaker: Unknown
en: With or without kids, at this stage of my company, at this stage of my career, whatever it is, at this age, how much sleep do I need in order to feel awesome, good enough, or it's not enough?
zh: 有没有孩子，在我的公司的这个阶段，在我职业生涯的这个阶段，不管是什么，在这个年龄，我需要多少睡眠才能感觉状态极佳、够好，还是不够？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think most people know that.
zh: 而且我认为大多数人都知道这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, so that's step number one.
zh: 好，这就是第一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: The next one is something most people don't ever talk about, which is some people actually just have more energy.
zh: 下一步是大多数人从来不谈的事情，那就是有些人天生就拥有更多的能量。

speaker: Unknown
en: They can focus for long, long periods of time.
zh: 他们能够长时间、长时间地保持专注。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have a ton of energy to run.
zh: 他们有大量的精力去跑步。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have a ton of energy to then go work.
zh: 他们有大量的精力再去工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what we never ask is, what is that person's internal state?
zh: 但我们从来不问的是，那个人的内在状态是什么样的？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I know people that can do all of that, but they're kind of redlining, and they're using a lot of stimulants to do it.
zh: 所以我认识一些人，他们能做到所有这些，但他们其实是在红线边缘运转，而且他们在使用大量兴奋剂来做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or they're not using stimulants to do it, but they're redlining.
zh: 或者他们没有使用兴奋剂来做到这一点，但他们是在红线边缘运转。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then at night, they're having a hard time switching it off, and so they're not resetting their system.
zh: 然后到了晚上，他们很难把状态关掉，所以他们没有让自己的系统复位。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some people, however, are these like wake up at 4 a.m., work out.
zh: 然而，也有一些人是那种早上 4 点起床、锻炼身体。

speaker: Unknown
en: Handle business, deal with family, go off to work, back to business, come home, and they pivot and task switch really fast.
zh: 处理事务、照顾家庭、出门上班、再回来处理事务，而且他们转换和切换任务非常快。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think these things are necessarily stable features throughout our entire life.
zh: 我不认为这些东西必然是我们整个一生中都稳定不变的特征。

speaker: Unknown
en: It seems to be a lot of young guys come up to me and they're like, what should I do?
zh: 似乎有很多年轻人来找我，他们会说，我该怎么做？

speaker: Unknown
en: The Oracle said it best, like, know thyself.
zh: 神谕说得最好，就是，认识你自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: You really have to be honest with yourself.
zh: 你真的必须对自己诚实。

speaker: Unknown
en: about what you need in order to do something for a long period of time.
zh: 关于你需要什么才能在很长一段时间内做某件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now that said, I do recall working 80, even 100 hour weeks in graduate school and that served me well.
zh: 话虽如此，我确实记得在读研究生时每周工作 80 甚至 100 个小时，而这对我很有帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, eventually led me to tenure at Stanford, et cetera.
zh: 我是说，这最终让我在 Stanford 拿到了终身教职，等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do think that if you can pull it off, I think from zero to maybe first four years of starting a company,
zh: 我确实认为，如果你能做到的话，我认为从零到创办公司的头四年左右，

speaker: Unknown
en: Or if you're in medical school, the goal is don't die.
zh: 或者如果你在医学院，目标就是别死掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Get as much done as you can and don't impair yourself with an injury or chronic disease.
zh: 尽可能多地完成事情，不要因为受伤或慢性疾病而损害自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't really define this thing, optimization.
zh: 我们其实并没有定义这个东西，优化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you start to pivot into how can I insert components of rest along the way, maybe during the day or across the week or the month that really allow me to access my best levels of focus and creativity.
zh: 然后你开始转向，如何在过程中插入休息的组成部分，也许在一天当中，或者跨一周、跨一个月，真正让我能够达到我最佳的专注力和创造力水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I'd be naive and I'd be lying if I said somebody's starting a company in the AI realm in the Bay Area or elsewhere these days.
zh: 但如果我说，如今某人在湾区或其他地方创办一家 AI 领域的公司，

speaker: Unknown
en: You're going to sit them down and you go, listen, you really need eight hours of sleep.
zh: 你会让他们坐下来，然后说，听着，你真的需要 8 个小时的睡眠。

speaker: Unknown
en: You got to do your resistance training.
zh: 你得做你的抗阻训练。

speaker: Unknown
en: You should do some breath work.
zh: 你应该做一些呼吸练习。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, no, none of that.
zh: 比如，不，这些都不用。

speaker: Unknown
en: What they should determine is how much energy they actually have.
zh: 他们应该确定的是，他们实际上拥有多少能量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you've met these people, right?
zh: 而且你见过这样的人，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Occasionally you'll run into like a Jimmy Iovine or some of the folks doing AI at Meta, and they just seem to have an extra gear.
zh: 偶尔你会遇到像 Jimmy Iovine 或者 Meta 里做 AI 的一些人，他们似乎就是多有一个挡位。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some people have this extra gear.
zh: 有些人有这种额外的挡位。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, there's one other component we can deep dive into any of these that nobody talks about.
zh: 现在，还有一个组成部分我们可以深入探讨，但没有人谈论它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's the ability to switch off your thoughts, your planning and your concerns at the end of your day and drop into sleep.
zh: 那就是在你一天结束时关掉你的念头、你的计划和你的忧虑，然后坠入睡眠的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can we go deeper in that one?
zh: 我们能在这个点上再深入一点吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because to be very selfish about it, if I was to self-diagnose, the biggest problem I have is downshifting.
zh: 因为说得很自私的话，如果让我自我诊断，我最大的问题就是降挡。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes we'll take literally four hours to go from a crazy, exciting, awesome day to literally even be able to fall asleep or just like stop the mind.
zh: 有时候我们会真的花上四个小时，才能从一个疯狂、兴奋、精彩的一天，真正过渡到能够入睡，或者只是让大脑停下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I could bestow myself with any gift, it would be what you're describing.
zh: 如果我能给自己任何一份礼物，那就是你所描述的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the research there of how to do that?
zh: 关于如何做到这一点，相关的研究是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: So in terms of sleep, there are a couple of prerequisites for sleep.
zh: 就睡眠而言，有几个前提条件。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are a bunch of don'ts.
zh: 有一堆「不要做」的事项。

speaker: Unknown
en: So obviously, you don't want to drink caffeine too late.
zh: 显然，你不想太晚摄入咖啡因。

speaker: Unknown
en: Being under too much bright light late in the day can make it difficult, but a lot of us can't control that.
zh: 一天中太晚接触过强的光线会造成困难，但我们很多人无法控制这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Alcohol, cannabis, these things impair the quality of your sleep, help you get to sleep.
zh: 酒精、大麻，这些东西会损害你的睡眠质量，帮助入睡。

speaker: Unknown
en: We all know that by now.
zh: 我们现在都知道这一点了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in terms of being able to turn your thoughts off.
zh: 但就能够关掉你的思绪而言。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a very, very difficult thing for people for good reasons.
zh: 出于充分的理由，这对人们来说是非常非常困难的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: The brain wants to think, plan, remember, and organize itself around what's coming next because such a huge aspect of brain function is a prediction of what's happening next.
zh: 大脑想要思考、计划、记忆，并围绕接下来要发生的事情来组织自己，因为大脑功能的一个巨大方面就是对接下来会发生什么的预测。

speaker: Unknown
en: So first requirement, turn your thoughts off.
zh: 所以第一个要求是，关掉你的思绪。

speaker: Unknown
en: Second requirement is slow your heart rate down.
zh: 第二个要求是放慢你的心率。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, so that's purely of body.
zh: 好的，那纯粹是身体层面的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then third is you need to forget about the position of your limbs in space.
zh: 第三是你需要忘记你的四肢在空间中的位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's work through each one systematically.
zh: 那么让我们系统地逐一处理。

speaker: Unknown
en: For the first one, turning your thoughts off is a skill.
zh: 对于第一个，关掉思绪是一种技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can think, we can predict, we can remember, but we also can get into pure sensation.
zh: 我们可以思考、可以预测、可以记忆，但我们也可以进入纯粹的感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's the gateway to turning off your thoughts.
zh: 而那就是通往关掉思绪的大门。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this doesn't come from Eastern tradition per se, although this has been discussed for a long time in those traditions, but there's a neuroscience correlate to all of this, of course, and we can talk about those.
zh: 这本身并非来自东方传统，尽管这些传统中对它已经讨论了很长时间，但当然，这一切都有神经科学的对应物，我们可以谈谈那些。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how do you do that?
zh: 那么你要怎么做呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to focus on pure sensation.
zh: 你必须专注于纯粹的感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you start focusing on the surface of your body.
zh: 所以你开始专注于你身体的表面。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you can detect your heart rate, some people are very good at what's called interoception.
zh: 如果你能觉察到你的心率，有些人非常擅长所谓的内感受。

speaker: Unknown
en: They can actually get pretty accurate measurements of their heart rate without pressing on a vein or artery.
zh: 他们实际上可以在不按压静脉或动脉的情况下，相当准确地测出自己的心率。

en: A big problem now is how important is it to understand the natural patterns of activity in detail before we start poking around and stimulating with writing?
zh: 现在一个大问题是：在我们开始乱戳并用写入进行刺激之前，详细理解天然的活动模式到底有多重要？

speaker: Unknown
en: And obviously, there are two ways to write, at least two.

speaker: Unknown
en: You can use pharmacology.
zh: 你可以使用药理学。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what does most pharmacology do, whether it's alcohol, barbiturates?
zh: 那么大多数药理学在做什么呢，无论是酒精、巴比妥类药物？

en: Sedatives of some kind, what are you doing?

speaker: Unknown
en: You're increasing the threshold for activation.
zh: 你在提高激活的阈值。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're quieting the brain by just increasing the threshold for activation.

en: You're doing it indirectly by increasing inhibitory release, so there's less excitation overall.

en: Because those generally work by increasing neuromodulators that increase the likelihood that neurons will fire.

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're just kind of ramping up that baseline.

en: You're sort of creating higher RPM across the brain and body.

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why they lead to some shaking, some agitation, like everything's like primed to move, primed to fire, primed to think.

speaker: Unknown
en: It's hard to shut off your mind when you're under the influence of stimulants.
zh: 在兴奋剂的作用下，你很难让脑子停下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Easier when you're under the influence of these other drugs that increase inhibition.
zh: 而在那些增加抑制的药物作用下就更容易一些。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the real question for trying to...
zh: 所以真正的问题在于……

speaker: Unknown
en: Get to better reading and writing to the nervous system is about spatial and temporal precision and how willing you are to put something underneath the skin.
zh: 实现更好的神经系统读写，关键在于空间和时间精度，以及你有多愿意把东西放到皮肤下面。

speaker: Unknown
en: I say skin because you don't necessarily have to go under the skull.
zh: 我说的是皮肤，因为你不一定非要钻到颅骨下面去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, let's take vagal stimulation, for example.
zh: 比如，拿迷走神经刺激来说。

speaker: Unknown
en: Vagal stimulation most people think about as a way to calm down, but most of the vagal pathways are excitatory.
zh: 大多数人认为迷走神经刺激是一种让人平静下来的方式，但大多数迷走神经通路其实是兴奋性的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so common treatments for depression now, if somebody's willing, is to put a small, a little smaller than a penny-sized stimulator under the skin of the neck and stimulate the vagus in order to overcome this sort of sedation that accompanies depression.
zh: 所以现在抑郁症的常见疗法，如果患者愿意的话，是在颈部皮肤下植入一个比一便士还小一点的刺激器，刺激迷走神经，以克服伴随抑郁症的那种镇静状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: So vagal stimulation increases alertness.
zh: 所以迷走神经刺激能提升警觉性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Neuroscientists have known this for a long time.
zh: 神经科学家早就知道这一点了。

en: And a lot of people are getting pretty good.

en: Results in their treatment of their depression by increasing vagal stimulation.

zh: 我的同事 Carl Deisseroth——在世最伟大的生物工程师之一——讲过一件不可思议的事：他在和一位有自杀倾向的抑郁症患者交谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then he starts increasing the stimulation on her vagus.
zh: 然后他开始增加她迷走神经上的刺激。

speaker: Unknown
en: And she starts moving from that to a discussion about how she feels willing enough to go out and apply for a job in real time.
zh: 她开始从那种状态转变，实时地开始谈论她觉得自己有足够的意愿出门去申请一份工作了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That just tells you that these excitatory mechanisms and these depressive mechanisms or inhibitory mechanisms are profound in terms of our perception of the outside world, our perception of ourself.
zh: 这就告诉你，这些兴奋性机制和这些抑郁性机制或抑制性机制，就我们对外部世界的感知、对自身的感知而言，影响是深远的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this would be very nice to have.
zh: 所以拥有这样的技术会非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: The question is, are you willing to go under the skin?
zh: 问题是，你愿意到皮肤下面去吗？

en: I am a guy that came up, not mainly through my lab, but he spent some time in my lab.

speaker: Unknown
en: He's now the head neurosurgeon at Neuralink, Matt McDougall, amazing guy, has a little receiver implanted under his skin of his hand between his thumb and his index finger.

speaker: Unknown
en: And it opens their door.
zh: 它可以打开他们的门。

en: To their home, to Keys.

en: I was like, what are you doing?
zh: 我当时就想，你们在干什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like some sort of biohacking Bay Area-ish kind of stuff.

en: He's like, yeah, like I'm just playing with the idea of what is it like to have a small device under your skin that can do stuff in the world for you?

en: But I think within 12 months, 20% of the entrepreneurial world will be

en: And that's coming next.
zh: 而这就是接下来会到来的东西。

zh: 人们在想的是多肽，我们要做什么？

zh: 我不担心多肽。

zh: 我想植入式设备才是接下来的方向。

zh: 市售的迷走神经刺激器，有一些显示出了一些前景。

en: But I will say there's some interesting results there, but we're not quite there.
zh: 但我要说，那里确实有一些有趣的结果，不过我们还没到那一步。

zh: 但想想 10 年前。

zh: 如果我告诉你，听着，你将会戴一枚戒指或者手腕上的一个手环，来测量你的睡眠和 HRV，那在当时是相当超前的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm so fascinated by this.
zh: 我对此非常着迷。

zh: 所以，有读取，以不同的保真度读取大脑的底层活动。

zh: 有写入。

zh: 视网膜、耳蜗、舌头、嗅觉系统、皮肤、神经肌肉控制——虽然神经肌肉控制不算在外周，但我认为我们对神经系统的运作方式了解得相当透彻。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we know how different wavelengths of light are transformed into visual images at a, not even a first approximation, but we understand that in significant detail, how motion is processed.
zh: 而且我们知道不同波长的光是如何被转换成视觉图像的，这甚至不只是初步近似，我们对它的理解相当深入，包括运动是如何被处理的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We understand a fair amount about memories, although I want to put that on the shelf for a moment because there's an important finding in the memory field that will make you feel like it's in kind of twilight zone, perhaps in neuroscience.
zh: 我们对记忆的理解也相当多，不过我想先把这一点搁置片刻，因为记忆领域有一个重要发现，可能会让你感觉有点像处于某种神经科学的暮光地带。

speaker: Unknown
en: It worries me all the time.
zh: 这一直让我很担忧。

speaker: Unknown
en: The hypothalamus, so circuits that are deep in the brain that control hunger, anger, sexual appetite, lack thereof, hormone secretion, those are switches.
zh: 下丘脑，也就是大脑深处那些控制饥饿、愤怒、性欲、性欲缺失、激素分泌的回路，那些是开关。

zh: 那么我们理解这些吗？

zh: 我们理解所有东西吗？

zh: 不。

zh: 但我们理解它们。

zh: 我是说，GLP 之所以如此有效、之所以获得如此大动能的原因之一，就是因为我们了解它们在大脑中的结合位置，它们当然会结合到这些下丘脑和其他区域，激活参与抑制食欲的神经元。

zh: 所以这其实是一个非常简单的等式。

en: You ramp these GLP levels up a thousandfold, people aren't as hungry.
zh: 你把这些 GLP 水平提高一千倍，人们就没那么饿了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it turns out they're not as driven for other things, too, if you get beyond a certain level.
zh: 但事实证明，如果超过某个水平，他们对其他事情的驱动力也会下降。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think Sam Altman talked about his experience with that at one point and why he decided to either back off the dosage or stop taking them.
zh: 我想 Sam Altman 曾谈到过他这方面的经历，以及他为什么决定要么减少剂量，要么停止服用。

speaker: Unknown
en: So as you move in from the periphery of the sensory organs, right?
zh: 那么，当你从感觉器官的外围往里走，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And as you move up from the base of the brain, the deeper limbic structures and hypothalamic structures to the prefrontal cortex, we can say, yeah, like your prefrontal cortex, we know based on lesion studies in humans, activation studies is really important for contextual learning, for strategy setting in different environments, for suppression of impulse, what we call top-down suppression.
zh: 而当你从大脑底部、更深层的边缘系统结构和下丘脑结构往上走到前额叶皮层，我们可以说，是的，比如你的前额叶皮层，我们基于人体的损伤研究和激活研究知道，它对情境学习、对不同环境中的策略设定、对冲动抑制——也就是我们所说的自上而下的抑制——非常重要。
